As of the [2020 United States census](2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), Arizona had a population of 7,151,502.[[2]](Demographics_of_Arizona#cite_note-2)

A past census found that the population had seen a natural increase since the last census of 297,928 people (that is 564,062 births minus 266,134 deaths) and an increase due to net [migration](Human_migration "Human migration") of 745,944 people into the state. [Immigration](Immigration_to_the_United_States "Immigration to the United States") from outside the United States resulted in a net increase of 204,661 people, and migration within the country produced a net increase of 541,283 people. New population figures for the year ending July 1, 2006, indicate that Arizona is the [fastest growing state in the United States](List_of_U.S._states_by_population_growth_rate "List of U.S. states by population growth rate"), with 3.6% population growth since 2005, exceeding the growth of the previous leader, <Nevada>. The most recent population estimates released by the US Census put the population at **7,278,717** in 2019.[[3]](Demographics_of_Arizona#cite_note-PopEstUS-3)

The population density of the state is 45.2 people per square mile.[[4]](Demographics_of_Arizona#cite_note-4) In 2010, there were an estimated 460,000 [undocumented immigrants](Undocumented_immigrants_in_the_United_States "Undocumented immigrants in the United States") in the state.[[5]](Demographics_of_Arizona#cite_note-5) These constituted an estimated 7.9% of the population.[[6]](Demographics_of_Arizona#cite_note-6)

The [center of population](Center_of_population "Center of population") of Arizona is located in [Maricopa County](Maricopa_County%2C_Arizona "Maricopa County, Arizona"),[[7]](Demographics_of_Arizona#cite_note-7) which contains over 61% of Arizona's population.

## Ancestry

### 2020 census

According to the 2020 census, the racial make up of Arizona was 53.4% [Non-Hispanic White](Non-Hispanic_White "Non-Hispanic White"), 4.7% [African American](African_American "African American"), 4.5% [Native American](Native_Americans_in_the_United_States "Native Americans in the United States"), 3.6% [Asian](Asian_people "Asian people"), .2% [Pacific Islander](Pacific_Islander "Pacific Islander"). The State was 30.7% [Hispanic or Latino](Hispanic_or_Latino "Hispanic or Latino").[[8]](Demographics_of_Arizona#cite_note-8)

While some of the native flora and fauna of the [Sonoran Desert](Sonoran_Desert "Sonoran Desert") can be found within Phoenix city limits, most are found in the suburbs and the undeveloped desert areas that surround the city. Phoenix has a [hot desert climate](Desert_climate#Hot_desert_climates "Desert climate") ([Köppen:](K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification "Köppen climate classification") *BWh*),[[15]](Phoenix%2C_Arizona#cite_note-ViennaKoppen-15)[[16]](Phoenix%2C_Arizona#cite_note-HESKoppen-16) typical of the [Sonoran Desert](Sonoran_Desert "Sonoran Desert"), and is the largest city in [America](Americas "Americas") in this climatic zone.[[109]](Phoenix%2C_Arizona#cite_note-109) Phoenix has long, extremely hot summers and short, mild winters. The city is within one of the world's sunniest regions, with its [sunshine duration](Sunshine_duration "Sunshine duration") comparable to the <Sahara> region. With 3,872 hours of bright sunshine annually, Phoenix receives the most sunshine of any major city on Earth.[[110]](Phoenix%2C_Arizona#cite_note-110) Average high temperatures in summer are the hottest of any major city in the United States.[[111]](Phoenix%2C_Arizona#cite_note-Farmers-111) On average, there are 111 days annually with a high of at least 100 °F (38 °C), including most days from the end of May through late September. Highs top 110 °F (43 °C) an average of 21 days during the year.[[112]](Phoenix%2C_Arizona#cite_note-NOAA-112) On June 26, 1990, the temperature reached an all-time recorded high of 122 °F (50 °C).[[113]](Phoenix%2C_Arizona#cite_note-113) The annual minimum temperature in Phoenix is in the mid-to-low 30s.[[112]](Phoenix%2C_Arizona#cite_note-NOAA-112) It rarely drops to 32 °F (0 °C) or below. Snow is rare.

Maricopa County, which includes Phoenix, was ranked seventh for most [ozone pollution](Tropospheric_ozone "Tropospheric ozone") in the United States according to the [American Lung Association](American_Lung_Association "American Lung Association").[[114]](Phoenix%2C_Arizona#cite_note-114) Vehicle emissions are cited as precursors to ozone formation. Phoenix also has high levels of [particulate](Particulates "Particulates") pollution; although, cities in California lead the nation in this hazard.[[115]](Phoenix%2C_Arizona#cite_note-115) PM2.5 particulate matter, which is a component of diesel engine exhaust, and larger PM10 particles, which can come from dust, can both reach concerning levels in Phoenix.[[116]](Phoenix%2C_Arizona#cite_note-116) In fact, people, pets, and other animals exposed to high concentrations of PM10 dust particles―primarily from dust storms or from disturbed agricultural or construction sites―are at risk of contracting [Valley Fever](Valley_Fever "Valley Fever"), a fungal lung infection.[[117]](Phoenix%2C_Arizona#cite_note-117)

Unlike most desert locations which have drastic fluctuations between day and nighttime temperatures, the [urban heat island](Urban_heat_island "Urban heat island") effect limits Phoenix's [diurnal temperature variation](Diurnal_temperature_variation "Diurnal temperature variation").[[118]](Phoenix%2C_Arizona#cite_note-118) As the city has expanded, average summer low temperatures have been steadily rising. Pavement, sidewalks, and buildings store the Sun's heat and radiate it at night.[[119]](Phoenix%2C_Arizona#cite_note-119) The daily normal low remains at or above 80 °F (27 °C) for an average of 74 days per summer.[[112]](Phoenix%2C_Arizona#cite_note-NOAA-112) On July 19, 2023, Phoenix set its record for the warmest daily low temperature, at 97 °F (36 °C).[[112]](Phoenix%2C_Arizona#cite_note-NOAA-112)

The city averages approximately 300 days of sunshine, or over 85% of daylight hours, per year,[[120]](Phoenix%2C_Arizona#cite_note-120)[[121]](Phoenix%2C_Arizona#cite_note-121) and receives scant rainfall―the average annual total at Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport is 7.22 in (183 mm). The region's trademark dry and sunny weather is interrupted by sporadic Pacific storms in the winter and the arrival of the [North American monsoon](North_American_monsoon "North American monsoon") in the summer.[[122]](Phoenix%2C_Arizona#cite_note-BATTG19-122) Historically, the monsoon officially started when the average [dew point](Dew_point "Dew point") was 55 °F (13 °C) for three days in a row—typically occurring in early July. To increase monsoon awareness and promote safety, however, the National Weather Service decreed that starting in 2008, June 15 would be the official "first day" of the monsoon, and it would end on September 30.[[123]](Phoenix%2C_Arizona#cite_note-123) When active, the monsoon raises humidity levels and can cause heavy localized precipitation, flash floods, hail, destructive winds, and [dust storms](Dust_storm#Dust_storm_visibility_of_¼_mile_or_less,_or_meters_or_less "Dust storm")[[124]](Phoenix%2C_Arizona#cite_note-124)—which can rise to the level of a [haboob](Haboob "Haboob") in some years.[[125]](Phoenix%2C_Arizona#cite_note-125)
